title: Move entity counts from committed grounding to live tools
context: Grounding blocks in 5 committed files auto-regenerate with volatile entity counts (decisions, bugs, constraints, etc.) on every branch. When parallel branches capture different counts, this creates real merge conflicts across all 5 files. The counts serve no programmatic purpose—tooling recomputes them on demand. Touches invariant(s): con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file).
decision: Removed auto-generated counts sentences from committed grounding blocks (.cursor/rules, .github, CLAUDE.md, etc.). Redirected readers to `hunch doctor` and `hunch now` for live, accurate counts computed at read time instead of cached snapshots.
consequences: Eliminates recurring merge conflicts on grounding block files across all 5 committed locations when branches diverge
Grounding blocks become stable and content-addressed—safe to cache, diff, and re-merge cleanly
Readers always see accurate, up-to-date counts from tooling rather than stale committed snapshots
Test signals shifted from 'counts line changes' to 'constraints list changes' for detecting content updates
Removed end-to-end test scenario (grounding-merge-lag.test.ts) that relied on counts line regeneration
alternatives_rejected: Keep counts but suppress them during capture (masks the problem; adds coordinator friction)
Implement smarter merge resolution for the counts line (conflicts remain real, just resolved automatically)
Make counts deterministic per-branch (parallel branches genuinely have different entity counts—no way to avoid divergence)
